Claim 1 is believed to incorporate the relevant allowable
matter from claims 2 and 3. In particular, matter removed from claim 1 is believed to be redundant, or clarified, in light of adding the relevant allowable matter from claims 2 and 3. Claim 19
is allowable.
Han provides collision warnings provided by stationary
vehicles (Title). Sabeti provides VEHICLE VISION SYSTEM WITH IMAGE PROCESSING (Title). Danzl provides DEVICE AND METHOD FOR
CONTROLLING A MOTOR VEHICLE (Title). Nagy provides RADAR MODULE FOR USE WITH TRAFFIC MONITORING AND PREDICTIVE ANALYSIS SYSTEMS
(Title) .
In contrast, claim 11 of the presently claimed invention
provides an apparatus comprising a capture device and a processor.

The capture device may be configured to generate pixel data corresponding to an exterior of a vehicle. The processor may be configured to process the pixel data arranged as video frames, perform computer vision operations on the video frames to detect a moving object in the video frames, determine a predicted path of

the moving object, determine a probability of the moving object colliding with the vehicle based on the predicted path, determine a course correction to prevent the moving object from colliding with the vehicle, generate discrete steps to perform the course correction, and generate a control signal when the probability is greater than a pre-determined threshold. The control signal may be configured to enable an audio output played from the vehicle comprising a verbal instruction. The predicted path may be
determined by tracking the moving object over time in a sequence of video frames. The verbal instruction may comprise the discrete steps of the course correction. The discrete steps comprise
instructions for a driver of the moving object. The references, alone or in combination, do not teach or suggest each of these
limitations.
In particular, claim 11 provides that the control signal
may be configured to enable an audio output played from the vehicle comprising a verbal instruction and the verbal instruction may comprise the discrete steps of the course correction. The

combination of references is silent regarding the control signal configured to enable an audio output played from the vehicle comprising a verbal instruction, as claimed. At best, the primary reference, Han, describes human speech auditory warnings. Human speech auditory warnings are not the verbal instructions comprising the describe steps of the course correction as claimed. The Office

Action relies on Nagy to describe the discrete steps of the course correction. However, Nagy at [0024] describes a vehicle notification system 124B of another vehicle to direct that other vehicle. The vehicle notification system 124B in Nagy is described as including "a horn, speakers, interior lights, computer screen, or other devices within the target vehicle" (emphasis added). The claimed limitations describe that the audio output is played from the claimed vehicle to the moving object. In contrast, Nagy

describes sending an alert condition directly to a computer system of another vehicle and a device within the other vehicle would provide the audible notification to the driver of the other vehicle. The claimed invention describes the vehicle that would potentially be hit playing back the verbal instructions, while Nagy describes the vehicle that would potentially be doing the hitting would play the verbal instructions. Nagy teaches away from the control signal being configured to enable an audio output played from the vehicle comprising a verbal instruction and the verbal instruction may comprise the discrete steps of the course correction, as claimed. Sabeti does not cure the deficiencies of Han and Nagy. As such, the combination of references does not teach or suggest that the control signal may be configured to enable an audio output played from the vehicle comprising a verbal instruction and the verbal instruction may comprise the discrete
steps of the course correction, as claimed.
The references are silent regarding that the control

signal may be configured to enable an audio output played from the vehicle comprising a verbal instruction and the verbal instruction may comprise the discrete steps of the course correction, as claimed. Therefore, the claims include limitations not taught or suggested by the cited references and the rejection should be
withdrawn.
Claims 2, 4-10, and 12-18 depend either directly or
